text: The requirement for the traffic control device to be in the public domain shall not apply to individual components used in the assembly or manufacture of the traffic control device.
Does the rule that a traffic control device must not be proprietary also cover the individual parts it is built from?

A vendor is supplying flashing beacon assemblies to a county. The assembly design as a whole is non-proprietary, but the LED driver board inside it is patented by one manufacturer. The county also wants a two-year warranty. Can the patented internal part be used without breaking the manual's rules on proprietary devices?

The actions required of road users to obey regulatory devices should be specified by State statute, or in cases not covered by State statute, in local ordinances or resolutions. Such statutes, ordinances, and resolutions should be consistent with the “Uniform Vehicle Code.”
Where should the rules that say what drivers must do when they meet a regulatory device be written down?

A city is drafting an ordinance on what drivers must do at a new type of regulatory sign, because state law does not cover the case. The council also wants the ordinance published in two languages. Where should these driver duties normally be set out, and what should the ordinance be consistent with?

Unless otherwise defined in this Section, or in other Parts of this Manual, words or phrases shall have the meaning(s) as defined in the “Uniform Vehicle Code,” “AASHTO Transportation Glossary (Highway Definitions),” or other appropriate publications.
If a word used in the manual is not defined anywhere in it, where does its meaning come from?

An engineer and a contractor disagree about what a term in a traffic control plan means. The term appears in the manual, but the definitions section does not list it and no other Part defines it. The contract was signed in March. Which outside references does the manual point to for the meaning?
An additional W9-6 or W9-6e sign may be installed approximately 2 miles in advance of a mainline toll plaza. This sign may be either mounted overhead or post-mounted.
Can a second sign warning drivers to pay a toll or pull a ticket be placed farther ahead of a toll station, and how far?

A tollway is redesigning the approach to a mainline toll plaza where drivers must stop to pay or take a ticket. The existing advance sign is about one mile upstream, and the shoulder there is 10 feet wide. The designers want one more warning sign further out. Where may it go, and may it hang over the road?

The Emergency Medical Services (D9-13) symbol sign (see Figure 2I-1) may be used to identify medical service facilities that have been included in the Emergency Medical Services system under a signing policy developed by the State and/or local highway agency.
Is there a symbol sign that points drivers to emergency medical facilities, and when can it be used?

A rural county wants to post a blue symbol sign directing motorists to a clinic that belongs to the regional emergency medical services network. The clinic is open 24 hours and is 3 miles off the highway. Under what condition may the medical services symbol sign be used?

Highway agencies providing recreational and cultural interest area signing should establish a policy with signing criteria for the eligibility of the various types of services, accommodations, and facilities. These signs should not be used where they might be confused with other traffic control signs.
Before putting up brown signs for parks and attractions, what should a road agency have in place?

A state DOT is getting many requests from campgrounds, museums and ski areas for brown destination signs along a scenic route that carries about 4,000 vehicles a day. What should the agency set up before approving these signs, and where should it avoid using them?

Where vehicles are required to have a registered ETC account to use the lane, one or two flashing yellow beacons (see Section 4R.03) may supplement a canopy sign over an ETC Account-Only lane to call special attention to the location of the ETC Account-Only lane within the plaza.
Can flashing lights be added at a toll lane that only accepts drivers with an electronic toll account?

At a toll plaza, one lane is restricted to vehicles with a registered transponder account, and a sign on the canopy marks it. Drivers without accounts keep entering that lane. The plaza has six lanes. What device may be added to draw attention to that lane?

Regulatory, warning, and guide signs (see Section 2A.03), and object markers, shall be retroreflective or illuminated to show the same shape and similar color by both day and night, unless otherwise provided in this Manual for a particular sign or group of signs.
Do road signs have to look the same at night as in the daytime, and how?

A town wants to replace its signs with cheaper non-reflective panels and no lighting, arguing that few people drive at night on these streets. The signs include stop signs, curve warnings and street-name guide signs, and the budget is $40,000. Is that allowed?
The DO NOT DRIVE ON SHOULDER (R4-17) sign (see Figure 2B-10) may be installed to inform road users that using the shoulder of a roadway as a travel lane is prohibited.
Is there a sign that tells drivers not to use the paved edge of the road as an extra travel lane?

During rush hour, drivers on a suburban highway pass slow traffic on the right by driving on the paved shoulder. The shoulder is 8 feet wide and has rumble strips. What sign may the agency install to tell drivers this is not allowed?
Symbol designs shall in all cases be unmistakably similar to those shown in this Manual and in the “Standard Highway Signs” publication (see Section 1A.05).
Can an agency draw its own version of a sign symbol, such as a different-looking pedestrian figure?

A city's design team has redrawn the walking-person symbol on its crossing warning signs in a minimalist style to match the city's branding. The new signs would also use a slightly larger panel. Does the manual allow a symbol that looks noticeably different from the standard one?

When a Warning Beacon is interconnected with a traffic control signal or queue detection system, the BE PREPARED TO STOP sign should be supplemented with a WHEN FLASHING (W16-13P) plaque (see Figure 2C-16).
If a sign warning that drivers may have to stop has a flashing light tied to the signal ahead, what extra small sign should go with it?

On a 55 mph approach to a signalized intersection hidden behind a crest, an agency installed a BE PREPARED TO STOP sign with a beacon that flashes only when the signal is about to turn red. The sign is mounted 7 feet high. What should be added to the sign assembly?
If used, the WRONG WAY sign should be placed at a location along the one-way roadway farther from the crossroad than the DO NOT ENTER sign (see Section 2B.46).
On a one-way road, where should the sign telling drivers they are going the wrong direction go, compared with the sign telling them not to enter?

Drivers sometimes enter a freeway off-ramp from the crossroad going the wrong way. The ramp already has a DO NOT ENTER sign near the crossroad, and the agency is adding a WRONG WAY sign. The ramp is 900 feet long. Where along the ramp should the WRONG WAY sign go?

Optional Movement Lane Control (R3-6, R3-6a and R3-6b) signs (see Figure 2B-4), if used, shall be used for two or more movements from a specific lane or to emphasize permitted movements. The Optional Movement Lane Control sign shall be mounted overhead over the specific lane to which it applies.
A lane lets drivers either turn or go straight. If an arrow sign shows that, where does it have to be mounted?

At a four-lane signalized approach, the inside lane allows both left turns and through movements. The agency wants a sign with a combined left-and-through arrow for that lane. A median pole stands 5 feet from the lane. Can the sign go on the median pole, or where must it be mounted?
When Shelter Directional signs are used in an incident situation, such as during the aftermath of a nuclear or biological attack, the background color may be fluorescent pink (see Chapter 6O).
During a disaster, what background color can the signs pointing people to emergency shelters use?

After a chemical release, county emergency managers are putting up signs directing residents to shelters in three school gyms. They have orange, yellow and pink sign blanks in stock. Which background color does the manual allow for shelter directional signs in an incident?

When an Added Lane sign is to be installed on a roadway that curves before converging with another roadway that has a tangent alignment at the point of convergence, the Entering Roadway Added Lane (W4-6) sign (see Figure 2C-11) should be used to better portray the actual geometric conditions to road users on the curving roadway.
When a ramp curves before joining a straight road and gets its own new lane, which lane-added warning sign should drivers on the ramp see?

A loop ramp curves sharply and then joins a straight arterial, where the ramp traffic gets its own new lane instead of merging. The ramp's advisory speed is 25 mph. Which added-lane warning sign should be used on the ramp?

A Stop Ahead (W3-1) or Signal Ahead (W3-3) warning sign (see Section 2C.35) may be placed, where engineering judgment indicates a need, along the ramp in advance of the crossroad, to give notice to the driver.
At a diamond interchange, can a sign on the off-ramp warn drivers that a stop or a traffic light is coming at the cross street?

At a diamond interchange, the exit ramp ends at a stop sign at the crossroad, but the stop sign is hard to see because of a bridge pier. The ramp is 1,200 feet long and carries mostly trucks. What warning sign may be placed along the ramp?

Advance Guide and Exit Direction signs for exits to direct access ramps from a preferential lane should be mounted overhead. A Pull-Through sign over the preferential lane should be used with the Exit Direction sign at exits to direct access ramps.
For an exit that leaves directly from a carpool or express lane, should the guide signs be overhead or at the roadside?

An express toll lane in the median has its own exit ramp that drops directly to a cross street. The general-purpose roadway has four lanes in each direction. How should the advance and exit guide signs for that median exit be mounted, and what other sign should go with the exit sign?

To be recognized as a double line rather than two separate, disassociated single lines, the discernible space separating the parallel lines of a double line should not exceed two times the line width of a single line.
How far apart can the two stripes of a double line be before they look like two separate lines?
A contractor painted a double yellow center line with 4-inch stripes and a 12-inch gap between them. The road was resurfaced last year. Is that gap acceptable for the pair to read as one double line?

If used on the roadways of divided highways or one-way streets, or on any ramp in the direction of travel, left edge line pavement markings shall consist of a normal width solid yellow line to delineate the left-hand edge of a roadway or to indicate driving or passing restrictions left of these markings, except as provided in Section 3E.04.
On a one-way road, what color and pattern should the line along the left edge be?
A new freeway off-ramp is being striped. The designer drew solid white lines along both edges of the ramp. The ramp is 16 feet wide. Is that right for the left side?
Red delineators may be used on the reverse side of any delineator where it would be viewed by a road user traveling in the wrong direction on that particular ramp or roadway.
Can reflectors on the back of roadside posts show a color that warns drivers going the wrong way?

An agency has repeated wrong-way entries on a two-lane ramp. The ramp already has post-mounted reflectors on both sides facing correct-direction traffic. What may be placed on the back of those posts for drivers heading the wrong way?
Two-way left-turn lane markings should not extend to intersections (see definition in Section 1C.02).
Should the center turn lane markings shared by both directions run right up to the intersection?

A five-lane arterial has a continuous center lane for left turns from both directions. The resurfacing plan carries those markings all the way to the crosswalk at a signalized intersection. The speed limit is 40 mph. Is that how the markings should end?
If a pavement marking word message consists of more than one line of information, it should read in the direction of travel. The first word of the message should be nearest to the road user.
When words painted on the road take two lines, which line should drivers reach first?

A school zone gets a pavement message painted on two lines: SCHOOL and XING. The crew is debating which word to paint closer to approaching drivers. The lane is 11 feet wide. Which order should be used?
Crosswalk markings may be omitted if engineering judgment indicates they are not needed to direct pedestrians to the proper crossing path(s).
Is it always required to paint crosswalk lines where people cross, or can they be left out?

At a quiet residential intersection with stop signs on all four legs, pedestrians already cross along the obvious lines of the sidewalks. The street is 30 feet wide. Can the agency decide not to paint crosswalk markings there?
In each vertically-arranged signal face, all signal sections that display red signal indications shall be located above all signal sections that display yellow and green signal indications.
In a traffic light with the lenses stacked top to bottom, where do the red lenses have to be?

A contractor installed a vertical five-section signal face for a left-turn approach with the red arrow placed below a green ball to fit the housing. The pole is 18 feet tall. Is that arrangement allowed?
The design (including the phasing, operation, and timing) of new traffic control signals should be based on an engineering study of roadway, traffic, and other conditions.
What should the phasing and timing of a new traffic light be based on?

A city is installing a new traffic signal where a shopping center driveway meets an arterial. The council wants to copy the timing plan from a similar intersection across town to save money. The arterial carries 22,000 vehicles a day. What should the signal's design be based on?

On multi-lane approaches having posted or statutory speed limits or 85th-percentile speeds of 35 mph or less, either a pedestrian hybrid beacon face should be installed on each side of the approach (if a median of sufficient width exists) or at least one of the pedestrian hybrid beacon faces should be installed over the roadway.
On a slower street with several lanes, where should the faces of a pedestrian-activated red beacon be placed?

A city is installing a pedestrian hybrid beacon across a four-lane street posted at 30 mph that has a 12-foot raised median. The plan shows both beacon faces on the right side of the approach. How should the faces be placed instead?
When pedestrian signal heads are used, a WALKING PERSON (symbolizing WALK) signal indication shall be displayed only when pedestrians are permitted to leave the curb or shoulder.
When is the walk symbol on a pedestrian signal allowed to be shown?

At an intersection with a leading turn phase, the controller shows the walking person to pedestrians while turning vehicles still have a green arrow across that crosswalk. The crosswalk is 60 feet long. Is that allowed?
Regulatory, warning, and guide signs should be used at highway traffic signal locations as provided in Part 2 and as specifically provided elsewhere in Part 4.
Do the normal rules for road signs still apply at intersections with traffic lights?

An engineer argues that once an intersection has traffic signals, no lane-use, turn-prohibition or street-name signs are needed because the signal controls everything. The intersection has dual left-turn lanes. Which parts of the manual govern signs at signalized locations?

Adequate time should be provided to allow traffic to clear the narrow facility before opposing traffic is allowed to move. Engineering judgment should be used to determine the proper timing for the signal.
On a narrow stretch where the two directions take turns through one lane under signal control, how should the timing be set?

A 400-foot one-lane bridge is controlled by signals at each end so that the two directions alternate. Drivers complain that opposing traffic gets a green before the bridge is empty. The bridge is posted at 25 mph. What should the signal timing ensure?

Warning Beacons that are mounted on toll plaza islands, behind impact attenuators in front of toll plaza islands, and/or on toll booth pylons (ramparts) to identify them as objects in the roadway may be mounted at a height that is appropriate for viewing in a toll plaza context, even if that height is lower than the normal minimum of 8 feet above the pavement.
Can flashing beacons that mark toll booth islands be mounted lower than usual?

At a toll plaza, the agency wants flashing yellow beacons on the concrete islands between booths at about 4 feet high, so drivers see them under the canopy. Elsewhere on the highway, beacons are at least 8 feet up. Is the lower height permitted?

If not otherwise prohibited, steady red, yellow, and green turn arrow signal indications may be used instead of steady circular red, yellow, and green signal indications in a signal face on an approach where all traffic is required to turn or where the straight-through movement is not physically possible.
If every driver on an approach has to turn, can the traffic light show arrows instead of round lights?

A T-shaped approach from a parking garage exit forces all traffic to turn right or left, because there is no road straight ahead. The signal face currently shows circular red, yellow and green. The garage has 800 spaces. May arrows be used instead?

Insofar as practicable, the height and lateral placement of signal faces should comply with the requirements for other traffic control signals in accordance with Chapter 4D. They should be located no more than 50 feet in advance of the movable bridge warning gate.
How far ahead of a drawbridge gate can the traffic signals that stop traffic be placed?

A bascule bridge over a shipping channel has warning gates on each approach. The designer wants to put the stop signals 120 feet before the gates, at the end of a curve, so they are seen earlier. The bridge opens about 20 times a day. Is that location acceptable?

When scanning graphics (see Section 2A.04) of any type are used on a sign for support of driving automation systems, the scanning graphics shall not be visible to the human eye and the sign shall have no apparent loss of resolution or recognition for the road user.
Can a sign carry a machine-readable pattern for self-driving cars, and does it have to be invisible to people?

A state pilot project wants to add a printed QR-style pattern to speed limit signs so automated vehicles can read them. The pattern would show as a faint grid on the sign face. The pilot covers 30 miles. Does the manual allow this?

Engineering judgment (see Section 1D.03) used to determine traffic control device selection and placement should consider uniformity in application and location needed to support both the human driver and driving automation system technology.
When deciding where to put traffic devices, should engineers think about automated vehicles as well as human drivers?

A county is updating its sign placement policy. One engineer wants to vary sign positions corridor by corridor to suit local preference; another argues consistent placement helps both people and vehicle automation systems. The county maintains 600 miles of road. What should engineering judgment consider?

The various TTC provisions for pedestrian and worker safety set forth in Part 6 shall be applied by knowledgeable (for example, trained and/or certified) persons after appropriate evaluation and engineering judgment.
Who is allowed to apply the work zone rules that protect pedestrians and workers?

A small utility company wants its summer interns, who have had no traffic control training, to set the cones and pedestrian detour for a sidewalk excavation. The job will last two days. Does the manual put any requirement on who applies these provisions?
When an exit ramp is closed, an EXIT CLOSED sign panel with a black legend and border on an orange background should be placed diagonally across the interchange/intersection guide signs.
When a highway exit is shut for construction, what goes on the existing green exit signs?

A freeway exit ramp will be closed for three weeks while it is rebuilt. The overhead and roadside guide signs for that exit will stay in place. The detour adds 2 miles. What should be put on those guide signs, and how should it look?
Other warning signs should comply with the general requirements of color, shape, and alphabet size and series. The sign message should be brief, legible, and clear.
If a work zone needs a warning sign the manual does not show, what rules should it follow?

A road crew needs a warning sign for loose gravel after a chip seal, and no standard sign has the wording they want. They plan a long three-line message on a white rectangle. The job is on a 45 mph road. What should such a sign follow?

When a work space interferes with an entrance ramp, a lane may need to be closed on the freeway (see Figure 6P-44). A TTC zone in the entrance ramp may require shifting ramp vehicular traffic (see Figure 6P-44).
If road work blocks part of an on-ramp, what may need to happen on the main highway?

A contractor must rebuild the merge area of a freeway on-ramp, and the work space extends into the ramp's acceleration lane. The freeway has three lanes and carries 80,000 vehicles a day. What may be needed on the freeway and on the ramp?
The RAMP NARROWS (W5-4) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be used in advance of the point where work on a ramp reduces the normal width of the ramp along a part or all of the ramp.
Is there a warning sign for when road work makes a highway ramp narrower than normal?

Barrier placed for bridge deck repairs reduces an exit ramp from 16 feet to 12 feet wide for a month. The ramp has a 35 mph advisory speed. Which warning sign should be placed ahead of the narrowed section?
For traffic incidents, particularly those of an emergency nature, TTC devices on hand may be used for the initial response as long as they do not themselves create unnecessary additional hazards.
At a crash scene, can responders use whatever cones and signs they have in the truck at first?

A fire crew arrives first at a multi-vehicle crash on a rural highway at night. They carry a few cones and flares but no standard advance warning signs. The crash blocks one of two lanes. Can they use the devices they have for the first response, and with what limit?
Where multiple advance warning signs are needed on the approach to a transition and activity area, the ROAD WORK AHEAD (W20-1) sign should be the first advance warning sign encountered by road users.
When several warning signs are needed before a work zone, which one should drivers see first?

A lane closure on a 55 mph highway needs three advance warning signs: one about the lane ending, one about a flagger, and the general road work sign. The crew is unsure of the order. The closure is 2 miles long. Which sign should come first?

Parking and stopping regulatory signs may be used to prevent parked or waiting vehicles from blocking pedestrians’ views, and drivers’ views of pedestrians, and to control vehicles as a part of the school traffic plan.
Can parking restriction signs be used near a school to stop cars blocking the view of children crossing?

Parents waiting to pick up students park along both sides of the street near a school crosswalk, so drivers cannot see children stepping out. The street is 36 feet wide and the school has 700 students. What signs may be used, and for what purposes?

A Yield Here To (Stop Here For) School Crossing (R1-5a or R1-5c) sign (see Figure 7B-1) may be used, in accordance with the provisions of Section 2B.19, in advance of a marked crosswalk that crosses an uncontrolled multi-lane approach within school zones.
Near a school, can a sign show drivers where to yield at a crosswalk on a wide street with no signal?

A marked crosswalk in a school zone crosses a four-lane street with no stop sign or signal. Vehicles in one lane stop for children while vehicles in the next lane keep going. The crossing guard works only in the mornings. What sign may be placed ahead of the crosswalk?
The Diagnostic Team should review the findings of the engineering study and determine the appropriate measures to clear highway traffic from the grade crossing prior to the arrival of rail traffic.
When a railroad crossing is very close to an intersection, who decides how to keep cars from being stuck on the tracks?

Queues from a signalized intersection regularly back up across a nearby railroad crossing. An engineering study has been completed. The railroad runs 12 trains a day. Who should review the study and decide on measures, and what should those measures achieve?

The minimum mounting height for post-mounted signs adjacent to pathways and sidewalks should be 4 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pathway or sidewalk surface (see Figure 9A-1).
How high should a sign beside a walking path at a railroad crossing be mounted?

A shared-use path crosses a rail line, and the agency is posting signs next to the path on short posts so cyclists see them. The plan shows the bottom of the signs 3 feet above the path surface. The path is 10 feet wide. Is that height acceptable?

If supplemental pavement marking symbol(s) are placed between the Grade Crossing Advance Warning sign and the grade crossing, the downstream transverse line should be at least 50 feet upstream from the stop or yield line at the grade crossing.
If an extra railroad symbol is painted on the road closer to the tracks, how close can its last line be to the stop line?

On an approach to a railroad crossing, the agency is adding a second painted railroad symbol between the advance warning sign and the tracks. The symbol's last crossbar would end 30 feet before the stop line. The speed limit there is 35 mph. Is that spacing acceptable?

Section 9B.14 describes a Bicycles Allowed Use of Full Lane sign that may be used in addition to or instead of the shared-lane marking to inform road users that bicyclists might occupy the travel lane.
Instead of painting the bike-and-arrows symbol in a lane, is there a sign telling drivers that cyclists may use the whole lane?

A downtown street has 10-foot lanes, too narrow to share side by side, and the city painted shared-lane markings. Merchants want fewer pavement symbols. The street is posted at 25 mph. What sign could be used together with or instead of the markings?

Where the Bicycles Yield to Peds sign is supported by a yield line pavement marking (see Section 3B.19) to establish the yielding point, the sign and the pavement marking shall be installed adjacent to each other.
If a sign telling cyclists to yield to people walking is paired with a painted yield line, where must the sign be placed?

On a busy shared path, the agency is adding a sign telling bicyclists to yield to pedestrians at a crossing point, along with a row of painted yield triangles. The plan puts the sign 40 feet before the triangles. The path carries 2,000 users a day. Is that placement correct?

A one-way frontage road meets a cross street, and drivers sometimes turn into it the wrong way. Which signs should mark the entrance to the one-way road at the cross street, and where should the sign farther along the road go relative to them?

At a toll plaza with one transponder-only lane, the agency wants flashing yellow lights at that lane's canopy sign and more flashing lights on the islands between booths, mounted low. What does the manual allow for each?

In a school zone, a marked crosswalk crosses a four-lane street with no signal. The agency wants a sign telling drivers where to yield to the children, and wants to know how far ahead of the crosswalk to place it and whether a painted line goes with it.
A shared-use path gets a sign telling cyclists to yield to pedestrians, plus a painted yield line. Where must the sign be relative to the line, and what should the painted yield line look like?
A city wants to tell drivers that cyclists may use the full lane on a narrow street, using a sign, pavement symbols, or both. What sign is that, and how does it relate to the painted symbols?

At a diamond interchange the exit ramp ends at a traffic signal hidden by a bridge pier. The agency wants a warning sign on the ramp. What sign may be used there, and what are the general rules for that kind of advance warning sign, such as an added plaque or beacon?

A freeway lets buses drive on the left shoulder during peak hours. What should the left edge line normally look like on a divided highway, and how do the markings change where part-time travel on the shoulder is allowed?
A new signal at a downtown corner will use vertical signal faces and pedestrian signals. In what order must the lenses be stacked, and when may the walking person be shown?

A freeway exit is closed for construction and a lane is closed ahead of it, needing several advance warning signs. Which advance warning sign should drivers meet first, and what goes on the existing exit guide signs?

Where a road and a sidewalk both cross a railroad, the agency is painting markings on the road approach and putting signs beside the sidewalk. How close to the stop line can an extra painted railroad symbol end, and how high should the sidewalk signs be mounted?
